subject.title: [Bug]: Preflight compaction failure permanently locks Composer into "terminated" state

question: Should this issue be fixed first by a narrowed runtime preflight retryability whitelist, by Control UI lifecycle recovery, or by both?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but related PR feedback shows the exact fail-open boundary is compatibility-sensitive because broad 4xx handling can hide auth or request-shape errors.

options.title: Narrow Runtime Whitelist
options.body: Treat timeout, 5xx, and any explicitly approved 429 case as skippable guardrail failures while keeping 400/401/403 and broad summary failures terminal, with positive and negative tests.

options.title: UI Lifecycle Recovery
options.body: Keep the runtime policy stricter and make `chat.dispatch-error` from preflight compaction restore the Composer with an actionable error, proven in Control UI.

options.title: Layer Both Defenses
options.body: Use the narrow runtime whitelist for true transient infrastructure failures and add UI recovery only as a safety net if proof shows a terminal dispatch can still wedge the Composer.

recommendation.title: Narrow Runtime Whitelist
recommendation.body: Treat timeout, 5xx, and any explicitly approved 429 case as skippable guardrail failures while keeping 400/401/403 and broad summary failures terminal, with positive and negative tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the live policy feedback on the related PRs and are the clearest owner signal for the retryability boundary.
